stanzas.sanskrit:
गत्वा सान्दीपनिमथ चतुष्षष्टिमात्रैरहोभिः
सर्वज्ञस्त्वं सह मुसलिना सर्वविद्या गृहीत्वा ।
पुत्रं नष्टं यमनिलयनादाहृतं दक्षिणार्थं
दत्त्वा तस्मै निजपुरमगा नादयन् पाञ्चजन्यम् ॥ ७६-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna went to Guru Saandipini ashram along with Balarama and mastered all arts in 64 days. As gurudakshina, Krishna brought back Guru's dead son alive from Yama's abode and gave back to the Guru and Guru's wife. Krishna returned back to Mathura sounding his Panchajanya conch.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
gatvā sāndīpanimatha catuṣṣaṣṭimātrairahobhiḥ
sarvajñastvaṃ saha musalinā sarvavidyā gṛhītvā |
putraṃ naṣṭaṃ yamanilayanādāhṛtaṃ dakṣiṇārthaṃ
dattvā tasmai nijapuramagā nādayan pāñcajanyam || 76-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
स्मृत्वा स्मृत्वा पशुपसुदृशः प्रेमभारप्रणुन्नाः
कारुण्येन त्वमपि विवशः प्राहिणोरुद्धवं तम् ।
किं चामुष्मै परमसुहृदे भक्तवर्याय तासां
भक्त्युद्रेकं सकलभुवने दुर्लभं दर्शयिष्यन् ॥ ७६-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The Gopikas in Vraja were always thinking of Krishna. Remembering their love, Krishna felt overwhelmed and decided to send Uddhava as a messenger to Gokulam, thereby creating an opportunity for Uddhava to understand the depth of devotion of the Gopikas.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
smṛtvā smṛtvā paśupasudṛśaḥ premabhārapraṇunnāḥ
kāruṇyena tvamapi vivaśaḥ prāhiṇoruddhavaṃ tam |
kiṃ cāmuṣmai paramasuhṛde bhaktavaryāya tāsāṃ
bhaktyudrekaṃ sakalabhuvane durlabhaṃ darśayiṣyan || 76-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वन्माहात्म्यप्रथिमपिशुनं गोकुलं प्राप्य सायं
त्वद्वार्ताभिर्बहु स रमयामास नन्दं यशोदाम् ।
प्रातर्दृष्ट्वा मणिमयरथं शङ्किताः पङ्कजाक्ष्यः
श्रुत्वा प्राप्तं भवदनुचरं त्यक्तकार्याः समीयुः ॥ ७६-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Uddhava reached Gokulam by evening. He spent the night with Nanda and Yashoda describing the great deeds of Krishna. In the morning, seeing the chariot, Gopikas thought Krishna had returned and later got to know that an emissary of Krishna has come. They came to meet Krishna's friend Uddhava,leaving away their works at home.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvanmāhātmyaprathimapiśunaṃ gokulaṃ prāpya sāyaṃ
tvadvārtābhirbahu sa ramayāmāsa nandaṃ yaśodām |
prātardṛṣṭvā maṇimayarathaṃ śaṅkitāḥ paṅkajākṣyaḥ
śrutvā prāptaṃ bhavadanucaraṃ tyaktakāryāḥ samīyuḥ || 76-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वा चैनं त्वदुपमलसद्वेषभूषाभिरामं
स्मृत्वा स्मृत्वा तव विलसितान्युच्चकैस्तानि तानि ।
रुद्धालापाः कथमपि पुनर्गद्गदां वाचमूचुः
सौजन्यादीन् निजपरभिदामप्यलं विस्मरन्त्यः ॥ ७६-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Gopikas saw Uddhava dressed in costumes and jewelry similar to Krishna. They were reminded of the leelas of Krishna. They forgot themselves and started to speak with choked voice.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
dṛṣṭvā cainaṃ tvadupamalasadveṣabhūṣābhirāmaṃ
smṛtvā smṛtvā tava vilasitānyuccakaistāni tāni |
ruddhālāpāḥ kathamapi punargadgadāṃ vācamūcuḥ
saujanyādīn nijaparabhidāmapyalaṃ vismarantyaḥ || 76-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
श्रीमन् किं त्वं पितृजनकृते प्रेषितो निर्दयेन
क्वासौ कान्तो नगरसुदृशां हा हरे नाथ पायाः ।
आश्लेषाणाममृतवपुषो हन्त ते चुम्बनाना-
-मुन्मादानां कुहकवचसां विस्मरेत् कान्त का वा ॥ ७६-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: They asked if the merciless Krishna sent Uddhava to just meet his parents, Nanda and Yashoda. They wanted to know about Krishna who must have become the beloved one for Mathura girls, by then. Unable to forget the nectar like body of Krishna and the embraces, the funny talks and actions and the love HE had given them, the Gopikas lamented that they cannot forget HIM.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
śrīman kiṃ tvaṃ pitṛjanakṛte preṣito nirdayena
kvāsau kānto nagarasudṛśāṃ hā hare nātha pāyāḥ |
āśleṣāṇāmamṛtavapuṣo hanta te cumbanānā-
-munmādānāṃ kuhakavacasāṃ vismaret kānta kā vā || 76-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
रासक्रीडालुलितललितं विश्लथत्केशपाशं
मन्दोद्भिन्नश्रमजलकणं लोभनीयं त्वदङ्गम् ।
कारुण्याब्धे सकृदपि समालिङ्गितुं दर्शयेति
प्रेमोन्मादाद्भुवनमदन त्वत्प्रियास्त्वां विलेपुः ॥ ७६-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Gopikas remembered how during Rasaleela dance, Krishna's beautiful hair had loosened and dishevelled while his body glowed with sweat drops. They requested Uddhava to tell Krishna that they wanted to embrace Krishna and experience it once again.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
rāsakrīḍālulitalalitaṃ viślathatkeśapāśaṃ
mandodbhinnaśramajalakaṇaṃ lobhanīyaṃ tvadaṅgam |
kāruṇyābdhe sakṛdapi samāliṅgituṃ darśayeti
premonmādādbhuvanamadana tvatpriyāstvāṃ vilepuḥ || 76-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
एवं प्रायैर्विवशवचनैराकुला गोपिकास्ताः
त्वत् सन्देशैः प्रकृतिमनयत् सोऽथ विज्ञानगर्भैः ।
भूयस्ताभिर्मुदितमतिभिस्त्वन्मयीभिर्वधूभि-
-स्तत्तद्वार्तासरसमनयत् कानिचिद्वासराणि ॥ ७६-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The Gopikas grief struck with Bhagwan’s absence. Uddhava comforted them with Bhagwan’s spiritual message. They came to their normal selves and experienced Bhagwan’s inner presence. Uddhava spent some days with Gopikas joyfully narrating about Krishna.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
evaṃ prāyairvivaśavacanairākulā gopikāstāḥ
tvat sandeśaiḥ prakṛtimanayat so’tha vijñānagarbhaiḥ |
bhūyastābhirmuditamatibhistvanmayībhirvadhūbhi-
-stattadvārtāsarasamanayat kānicidvāsarāṇi || 76-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वत्प्रोद्गानैः सहितमनिशं सर्वतो गेहकृत्यं
त्वद्वार्तैव प्रसरति मिथः सैव चोत्स्वापलापाः ।
चेष्टाः प्रायस्त्वदनुकृतयस्त्वन्मयं सर्वमेवं
दृष्ट्वा तत्र व्यमुहदधिकं विस्मयादुद्धवोऽयम् ॥ ७६-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Uddhava noticed that in Gokulam, only songs related to Krishna leelas were heard in every house when they did their household works. Their talks were always centered about Krishna. The people talked about Krishna even in their dreams. Their actions imitated Krishna as they tried to personify HIM . Uddhava was left wonderstruck and stunned by these observations.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvatprodgānaiḥ sahitamaniśaṃ sarvato gehakṛtyaṃ
tvadvārtaiva prasarati mithaḥ saiva cotsvāpalāpāḥ |
ceṣṭāḥ prāyastvadanukṛtayastvanmayaṃ sarvamevaṃ
dṛṣṭvā tatra vyamuhadadhikaṃ vismayāduddhavo’yam || 76-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
राधाया मे प्रियतममिदं मत्प्रियैवं ब्रवीति
त्वं किं मौनं कलयसि सखे मानिनीमत्प्रियेव ।
इत्याद्येव प्रवदति सखि त्वत्प्रियो निर्जने मा-
-मित्थं वादैररमयदयं त्वत्प्रियामुत्पलाक्षीम् ॥ ७६-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Next, Uddhava met Radha and told her, how Krishna was always reminded of her. Krishna would talk about things Radha liked, the way she use to talk. If Uddhava was silent anytime, Krishna would ask why he was silent like his Radha. By conveying these, Uddhava made the lotus eyed Radha very happy.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
rādhāyā me priyatamamidaṃ matpriyaivaṃ bravīti
tvaṃ kiṃ maunaṃ kalayasi sakhe māninīmatpriyeva |
ityādyeva pravadati sakhi tvatpriyo nirjane mā-
-mitthaṃ vādairaramayadayaṃ tvatpriyāmutpalākṣīm || 76-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
एष्यामि द्रागनुपगमनं केवलं कार्यभारा-
-द्विश्लेषेऽपि स्मरणदृढतासम्भवान्मास्तु खेदः ।
ब्रह्मानन्दे मिलति न चिरात् सङ्गमो वा वियोग-
-स्तुल्यो वः स्यादिति तव गिरा सोऽकरोन्निर्व्यथास्ताः ॥ ७६-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna's message through Uddhava to Radha and Gopikas was that HE was unable to come to vraja due to his committed works and not due to HIS reduced love for them. Their devotion towards HIM was increasing in their separation and hence there is no need to grieve. Krishna will meet them soon and bless them with the supreme bliss after which union or separation from HIM will mean the same to them. Hearing these assuring words, Gopikas were freed from grief.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
eṣyāmi drāganupagamanaṃ kevalaṃ kāryabhārā-
-dviśleṣe’pi smaraṇadṛḍhatāsambhavānmāstu khedaḥ |
brahmānande milati na cirāt saṅgamo vā viyoga-
-stulyo vaḥ syāditi tava girā so’karonnirvyathāstāḥ || 76-10 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
एवं भक्तिः सकलभुवने नेक्षिता न श्रुता वा
किं शास्त्रौघैः किमिह तपसा गोपिकाभ्यो नमोऽस्तु ।
इत्यानन्दाकुलमुपगतं गोकुलादुद्धवं तं
दृष्ट्वा हृष्टो गुरुपुरपते पाहि मामामयौघात् ॥ ७६-११ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Uddhava realised that the devotion of Gopikas were the rarest and best in the whole world. No one has ever heard or seen such devotion to Bhagwan. Uddhava felt that prostration to their feet is enough to attain salvation and returned to Mathura blissfully.
Bhattathiri prayed to Bhagwan to protect him from him afflictions.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
evaṃ bhaktiḥ sakalabhuvane nekṣitā na śrutā vā
kiṃ śāstraughaiḥ kimiha tapasā gopikābhyo namo’stu |
ityānandākulamupagataṃ gokulāduddhavaṃ taṃ
dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭo gurupurapate pāhi māmāmayaughāt || 76-11 ||
